question.text: What does Clause 8.4 of the IFSCA (AML, CFT and KYC) Guidelines mandate regarding certification?

answer.text: Officers and employees of Regulated Entities dealing with AML/CFT matters must obtain relevant NISM-IFSCA certification
Only the Principal Officer needs to be certified by NISM
Certification is optional and recommended but not mandatory
Only the Governing Body members need AML/CFT certification

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the IFSCA (Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing and Know-Your-Customer) Guidelines, certification of personnel who handle AML/CFT functions is treated as a baseline competency requirement. The relevant clause obligates officers and employees of Regulated Entities dealing with AML/CFT matters to obtain the relevant NISM-IFSCA certification, so that AML/CFT roles are staffed by individuals with demonstrated subject-matter knowledge of the IFSCA AML/CFT framework. The Trap: Limiting the requirement to only the Principal Officer or only Governing Body members understates the scope — the obligation extends to all relevant officers and employees engaged in AML/CFT activity. Treating the certification as "optional and recommended" contradicts the prescriptive nature of the IFSCA Guidelines on staff competency. Note: The cited pages of the NISM-IFSCA-01 workbook (pp. 6, 9, 77, 109, 126) describe the certification examination and identify section 8.4 in their own numbering as relating to FATF-Style Regional Bodies; they do not, in the pages checked, explicitly state that "Clause 8.4" of the IFSCA Guidelines mandates NISM-IFSCA certification for officers and employees. The framing above is general IFSCA-regulatory and certification-framework knowledge.
